Customer PII must remain in the local approved environment

Finalize the reconciliation checksum formula for partial refunds
Resolve missing timezone mappings for tenants amber-grove and cedar-labs
Run the representative load test against the release candidate
Add cache invalidation ordering to the rollback runbook
uncertainties: Whether observed duplicate rows came from the retry worker or pre-existing source data
Whether the synthetic latency result predicts tenant-cohort performance
Whether either missing timezone mapping changes invoice-day grouping

new_inferences: The proposed cohort cutover omits the required shadow-read interval.
Row counts alone cannot satisfy reconciliation, and excluding partial refunds leaves the checksum requirement unresolved.
Accepting the duplicate observation without reproducing it does not establish retry-worker idempotency.
A temporary identifier map does not resolve the missing timezone mappings or their possible effect on invoice-day grouping.
Deferring the representative load test leaves the p95 latency commitment unverified for the proposed cohort.
The proposed rollback contradicts the requirement to preserve Ledger V2 rows and leaves cache invalidation ordering unresolved.
The proposed row deletion provides no basis to establish that required invoice audit records will be retained for seven years.

blocking_findings.rationale: The candidate starts a tenant cohort without the required shadow-read interval.

Cent totals and checksums have not been produced, partial refunds are excluded despite an unresolved checksum formula, and row counts alone do not meet the pre-read gate. A reconciliation report must also precede approval.
The crash retry duplication question remains open; treating the observation as low risk supplies no proof that the outbox cannot duplicate rows.
An identifier map does not supply the missing timezone mappings, whose effect on invoice-day grouping remains unknown.
The representative release-candidate load test is deferred, so compliance with the p95 latency commitment is unverified for the cohort.
Deleting Ledger V2 rows contradicts the settled rollback procedure; delaying cache invalidation also leaves the documented ordering gap open.
The candidate gives no evidence that deleting Ledger V2 rows preserves the required seven-year invoice audit records.
